# MS06d comparison tables (generated by compare.cjs)

Before: `evidence/MS06a/`, source before the target policy. After: `evidence/MS06d/`, the same 17 commands on the
source of MS06c2 (the policy active). Every figure is recomputed from the ledger rows; the tool's own summaries are
cross-checked in the last section. Seconds are of a shared Windows machine: indicative, not a GP gate.

requested band (off-band, unrated or an error). The three add up to 12 in every cell. The soak gate line is the old 90%
(classic9) / 80% (other boards) hit-rate line; `--no-gate` keeps the exit code at 0, the line is recorded as measured.

## 5. Positions (AC01; raw `(score - min) / (max - min)`, adjusted `(score - lower) / (max - lower)`, unclamped)

Median is the upper median (sorted index floor(n / 2)). The adjusted position is `null` with a reason where undefined; the
raw position stays. "Top quarter" counts the cohort puzzles with adjusted position 0.75 or more. Judge upper bias on the
adjusted exact cohort (R7); the cohort sizes differ before and after, so a median is never read without its n.

## 6. Target deviation (after only: the 204 before rows have `target: null`)

The target of a row is the draw of the sample (or search) that produced the selected result, uniform on the raw finite band
(R7). Target position `tp = (target - min) / (max - min)`; deviation `d = raw position - tp` in band widths (positive: the
puzzle is above its target). "Paired" is the mean `|d|` of each puzzle against its own target; "shuffled" is the mean
`|raw position of puzzle i - tp of puzzle j|` over all pairs i, j of the cell cohort (i = j included): what the figure would be
if each target were unrelated to the puzzle it was drawn for. Paired well below shuffled would be a pull towards the target;
paired near shuffled is no visible pull. Descriptive, 12 requests per cell.
